title: Claude or Gemini?
author: Patient-Software-168
selftext:
I've been using chatgpt for a few months now but I cannot get being abused by open ai so I am thinking of continuing my work with another provider. 

  
I am doing a sim rts game with Codex, and are wondering if I should go with Claude or Gemini next. 

I keep hearing good about Claude for the most of it, but also heard that Gemini has a top tier model now. 

  
I am primarily looking for where I get most out of my 20 bucks. 

  
Also how hard is it for another model to pick up where the previous left?

comments.author: Kindly-Sail6260
comments.body:
Just use Claude. It’s the best for game development right now. The majority of devs in this sub use Claude and the comparisons all over YouTube just make it obvious that Claude is the better choice right now. Opus 5.5 at medium settings is all you need tbh. 

Just don’t one shot everything. If you are trying to take a game to market, build one system at a time. Make it good, make it find and move on. Best of luck!

replies.author: Patient-Software-168
replies.body:
Thanks. 

What's the best way to make Claude pick up where codex left

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: Tell it to read codex files on the projects. It’ll know where to pick up after you ask it to examine the game you made and it will offer changes so remember not just to let it run wild with what you have.

comments.author: Unhappy_Image973
comments.body: I do use Claude and it’s fantastic! I suggest it.

comments.author: TurnipHonest4037
comments.body:
Claude but it won't help you much with assets on 20 bucks.

Ideally you'll be making the assets yourself, otherwise you'll have to figure out a way to generate the assets with other models.

replies.author: Patient-Software-168
replies.body:
I am using a local comfy ui workflow but thanks for the heads up. 

What about rigging and animating though, I bet that also costs alot

replies.author: DaedalusRaistlin
replies.body:
Mixamo can do both, for humanoids, though it's a bit cumbersome. It's free though, so it's hard it beat in terms of value.

Personally I bought AutoRigPro when it was on sale, and I have Claude rig things in Blender. I use Kimodo for animations (which runs on the GPU, but doesn't need much - something like 3Gb VRAM.) 

I do image to model locally on my 3060TI 8Gb using the 8gb Trellis2 fork, plus my own fixes to limit system memory usage for a few seconds extra generation time. 

Claude still does a lot of it - breaking an image into pieces, running image to model on those, assembling the pieces together, and checking it matches the source image closely. It sets up the rigging and adds animations, and checks the result looks alright. Still needs a human eye to see things the screenshots it takes don't cover.

comments.author: jawni
comments.body: I'd be curious to know if any of the people who have commented have used Gemini 4 Neon, it's getting rave reviews. Sure Opus 5.5 is great, but I get the feeling most people recommending it haven't used the new Gemini models.

replies.author: Patient-Software-168
replies.body:
That is also what I am wondering about.

Neon should be the new nr 1 model, but I havent read anything about how much it cost to use

replies.author: giveen
replies.body: Neon on low is what I use for bug fixing.  I have AI Pro plan and its been fantastic for that. I also like the way it talks to me.

comments.author: Andress1
comments.body:
I prefer Sol 6.2 to Opus 5.5, it's similar but much faster and can generate high quality images. 

Unfortunately the usage is lower than Claude, but very worth it

comments.author: Strict_Title5189
comments.body: Never use claude way to fast burns tokens for similar results compared to chatgpt or Gemini

comments.author: caesium23
comments.body: Gemini is hot garbage. When it launched it was telling people to put glue on pizza, and it has only improved incrementally since. Those misleading "AI summaries" at the top of every Google search now? That's Gemini. It's an embarrassment.

comments.author: Annual_Power_5066
comments.body: i use both but id say gemini is better since neon

comments.body:

Look anywhere there is talk about frontier models and people are raving about the new Gemini models. No one who is using models for agentic purposes, except you, cares about the quality of the AI summaries because they know it isn't indicative of the frontier models' capabilities.
